summary: A person’s delight is what he gladly returns to, as the reader of Psalm 1 returns to Yahweh’s instruction. The same noun can name a purpose that is carried out or an affair with its appointed time. Job uses a similarly spelled verb for a movement of the tail.

senses.definition: The speaker recognizes Yahweh’s favor in his rescue from enemies. The person who fears Yahweh takes pleasure in his commands.

senses.gloss: wish or choose to do something
senses.definition: What one desires can be expressed in a choice or deed. Yahweh accomplishes what he desires and sends his word to do his will.

senses.gloss: pleasure or the object of pleasure
senses.definition: Psalm 1 shows the reader’s delight in instruction by his returning to it day and night. In Psalm 16 the speaker locates his delight among the holy ones.
The purpose of Yahweh prospers in his servant’s hand. Ecclesiastes uses the noun more broadly of an affair that has its appointed time.

senses.gloss: disposed to desire or welcome something
senses.definition: Psalm 34 asks who desires life, then restates the question in terms of loving days in which to see good.
Behemoth moves its tail like a cedar. The comparison evokes the strength of the movement, though the precise posture is uncertain.

words.summary: This physical movement is attested in a single description. The Arabic comparison suggests lowering or bending.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 773, art. خفض, n11111
evidence.note: The contrary is to raise something.

note: Most surfaces counted for bending are shared with the much commoner verb of delight. Job 40:17 is the evidence for the physical sense. The Arabic comparison bears only on this use. Ordinary instances of בָּהּ are also counted under the personal name by surface spelling.
